finding.claim: maxAge is not enforced when the token payload has no iat claim, so a validly signed token without iat is accepted regardless of age (until exp, or indefinitely if no exp).
finding.source: Signed token whose payload omits iat (issuer uses noTimestamp:true at src/signer.js:129 or an external issuer). Precondition: verifier configured with maxAge.
finding.sink: Age check: iat/maxAge validator pushed at src/verifier.js:648-650 and evaluated in verifyToken.

trace.note: maxAge validator pushed only when maxAge is a number
signature verified first, so the token must be issuer-signed
if (!(claim in payload)) continue skips the iat/maxAge validator when iat is absent
cacheSet mirrors the same skip, so cache bounds also ignore maxAge
noTimestamp:true omits iat from issued tokens

finding.guards_checked: Signature and algorithm allowlist enforced before claims (verifier.js:170, 177, 288). exp still enforced when present (verifier.js:638-646). Cache bounds consistent with validator. No bypass of signature.

finding.claim: The signature segment is not canonical-checked, so one token has several distinct valid strings (last base64url character's unused bits are ignored), breaking any denylist, replay or one-time-use logic keyed on the raw token string.
finding.source: Any holder of a valid token. Precondition: application keys revocation/replay state on the raw token string.
finding.sink: Buffer.from(signature,'base64') in signature verification (src/crypto.js:394), used by the HMAC comparison at src/crypto.js:398.

trace.note: BASE64URL_RE only checks the alphabet
signature segment passes the alphabet check; no trailing-bit canonical check
signature returned as-is; signed input is header.payload only
base64 decode ignores unused trailing bits, so variant characters yield identical bytes
timingSafeEqual on decoded bytes passes for each variant
verifySignature accepts the variant token

finding.guards_checked: Alphabet check (decoder.js:41). timingSafeEqual on decoded bytes (crypto.js:398). Signed input covers header and payload exactly, so only the signature segment varies. Comment at decoder.js:5-9 and 32-34 claims canonical rejection, which the code does not enforce.

finding.claim: When caching is enabled, a Buffer token makes cacheKeyBuilder (hashToken) call token.split, which Buffer lacks, so verify throws a TypeError synchronously instead of returning a TokenError.
finding.source: Raw Buffer token from the application (e.g. an untouched request body). Precondition: cache option enabled.
finding.sink: cacheKeyBuilder(token) at src/verifier.js:372 invoked before the decode try block, reaching token.split in src/utils.js:46.

trace.note: Buffer token accepted by type check
cache.get(cacheKeyBuilder(token)) runs outside the decode try block
hashToken calls token.split on a Buffer, which throws TypeError

finding.guards_checked: Cache is off by default: createCache returns null for undefined size (verifier.js:94-97). Availability impact only; no authentication bypass.

finding.claim: When all configured algorithms are HS*, a PEM public key is used as a raw HMAC secret, so an attacker who knows the public key can forge HS256 tokens.
finding.source: Developer configuration algorithms:['HS256'] (or other HS-only list) with a PEM public key as key. The public key is public. Attacker supplies a token with alg HS256.
finding.sink: HMAC verification with the PEM text as secret: createSecretKey at src/verifier.js:556 then createHmac at src/crypto.js:398.

trace.note: HS-only provided list returns before any PEM detection, so the key is never checked as a public key
detectPublicKeyAlgorithms called with the HS-only allowlist
prepareKeyOrSecret with isSecret=true converts the PEM text to a secret KeyObject
HMAC computed over the token with the public PEM as key

finding.guards_checked: No library guard in the HS-only path. Mixed lists are safe because createHmac rejects asymmetric KeyObjects (crypto.js:397-401 returns false). The behaviour is deliberate (comment at crypto.js:315), so this is a configuration footgun, not a code defect. Verdict PLAUSIBLE.

finding.claim: With caching enabled, a successful verification is cached by token hash and returned without re-fetching the key, so a token signed by a rotated or removed key stays accepted until min(exp, cacheTTL) (default 600000 ms).
finding.source: Holder of a token signed by a key that is later rotated or removed. Precondition: cache enabled and an async key lookup.
finding.sink: Cache hit returns success before the key lookup at src/verifier.js:439 (getAsyncKey).

trace.note: successful result cached under hashed token
cache checked before any key lookup
cache hit returns cached success while now is within bounds
key function not invoked on a cache hit, so revocation is not seen

finding.guards_checked: Cache disabled by default. Entry bounded by exp and cacheTTL (verifier.js:131-140). Behaviour is a documented trade-off of caching, so low severity.
